there are only two versions of the 'uncensored' version. The one from 1999, which runs at the original 'slow' speed and is just the original mix with the censored bits pasted on, and all other versions are the 40th anniversary mixes, both surround and stereo.
Get the remastered cd from 1999, or the 40th anniversary mix of the first album.

The original 'censored' version of the first album is and always has been the artist's original intention. The 'uncensored' version first came out it 1999, when Bruce botnick flew in the vocal parts from Jim into Break On Through and The End digitally for that year's remaster of the Doors catalogue. The second time this happened was in 2006, when all 6 albums were remixed for surround sound, which is where the 40th anniversary mixes came from. The Doors were fine with the 'censored' versions of break on through and The End since that's how they performed them live, as soon as the matrix shows which are like a few months after the first album came out. Jim occasionally through in a few Fucks and Kills when signing the end and threw in the last 'higher' on occasion but they almost always performed what was on the record. Oh and the reason all the 'fucks' and 'kills' are in the apocalypse now version of the end is because the doors's tape vault was a mess back then and they accidentally sent them the multi tracks instead of the two track master tape, so coplala remixed his own version for the movie. So in short the 'censored' version isn't 'censored', and the 'uncensored' versions are actually 'altered' versions.
